questions: C1: The brief gives no reference values for L, k, rho, c_p, q and T_0. Do you accept the unit case (all equal to 1 in SI units, so Q = 1) that I recommend? All reference numbers in spec_problem.md are provisional until you decide.
C2: Should negative q (a heat sink) be allowed? I recommend allowing any real q in the code and testing with q > 0. The parabola test holds for any sign; only the stated range of T assumes q >= 0.
Do you approve the notation table, including the dimensionless variables xi, tau, theta and the group Q = qL^2/(k T_0)? It becomes locked once you approve it.
summary: I wrote the M1 scope for the toy 1D heat problem. Conduction, the uniform source and heat storage are in; everything else is out, as the brief decides. The time scale is L^2/kappa; the slowest mode decays to 1 % after about 0.47 L^2/kappa, which sets how long the steady-state test must run. With theta = (T−T0)/(qL^2/k), the equation has no parameters, and the one dimensionless group is Q = qL^2/(k T0); the peak temperature rise is Q/8 = 0.125 of T0 in the reference case. No paper is cited, so citations.json is empty. The reference values rest on choice C1 (unit case), which you still need to decide.
